package_info.why_malicious: The package masquerades as the legitimate 'browserify' library but contains a malicious postinstall script that extracts and executes a persistent ELF binary. This binary performs extensive system reconnaissance, exfiltrates sensitive information to an attacker-controlled domain, seeks elevated privileges, and attempts destructive actions such as wiping /etc/ and disabling system services. The package abuses legitimate open-source components to evade detection and has a zero detection rate on VirusTotal.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Runs a Node.js script, then executes a binary extracted from an archive, and deletes the evidence (the bin directory).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The postinstall script executes a binary and then deletes its own installation files, which is highly unusual for legitimate packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not execute native binaries or remove their own files post-install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may run postinstall scripts for setup, but rarely execute binaries or self-delete.
key_indicators: Deletes installation artifacts immediately after execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ELF binary 'run' extracted and executed; uses 'sudo-prompt' to request root privileges
malicious_snippets.code_language: ELF binary (compiled, uses Node.js modules internally)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Extracts itself, requests elevated privileges, copies itself to /etc/rot1 for persistence, and runs on every boot.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Requests root privileges immediately after install, persists itself in a system directory, and ensures execution on every boot.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not install persistent binaries in /etc/ or require root access during install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System management tools may request elevation, but not via npm postinstall.
key_indicators: Ensures execution on every system boot

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Uses 'systeminformation' npm module to collect system/user/hardware info; exfiltrates via HTTP GET to 'ejemplo.me'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Performs extensive system fingerprinting (user, OS, Docker, Bluetooth, VM, CPU, RAM, disk, network, USB, etc.) and exfiltrates data to an attacker-controlled domain over plaintext HTTP.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Collects a wide range of sensitive system information and sends it to an external, attacker-controlled domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not exfiltrate system reconnaissance data to unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry in some enterprise software, but not to suspicious or non-standard domains.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attempts to remove /etc/ contents and disables systemctl/systemd services
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Attempts destructive actions: wipes /etc/ directory and disables critical Unix services, potentially bricking the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Destructive behavior targeting critical system directories and services.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should ever attempt to delete /etc/ or disable system services.

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package, triggering the postinstall script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Extraction and execution of the malicious ELF binary.

attack_chain.action: The ELF binary is extracted and executed, requesting elevated privileges via sudo-prompt.
The binary copies itself to /etc/rot1 for persistence and ensures execution on every boot.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing malicious activity on the system.

attack_chain.action: Performs system reconnaissance and exfiltrates data to attacker-controlled domain.
Attempts destructive actions: wipes /etc/ and disables system services (conditional).
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential system bricking or denial of service.

behavioral_signatures: npm postinstall script executes a native binary
Immediate deletion of installation artifacts (bin directory) after execution
Binary requests root privileges via sudo-prompt during install
Persistence by copying binary to /etc/rot1 and running on boot
Reconnaissance and exfiltration of system information to external domain
Attempts to delete /etc/ or disable systemctl/systemd
file_indicators: Presence of bin/run.tar.xz archive in npm package
Extraction and execution of ELF binary named 'run'
Immediate removal of ./bin directory after install
network_indicators: HTTP GET requests to 'ejemplo.me' with system fingerprinting data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that execute binaries and immediately delete installation files. Flag packages that extract and run ELF binaries, especially those requesting root privileges via sudo-prompt. Watch for persistence mechanisms involving /etc/rot1 or similar locations. Detect outbound HTTP requests to suspicious domains such as 'ejemplo.me', especially those containing system reconnaissance data. Alert on any process attempting to delete /etc/ or disable systemctl/systemd services.
